body.statement: Fix \(\delta\in[0,1]\) and suppose \(\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\neq\varnothing\). Then \(\max_{x\in\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)}c_\omega^{\top}x<0\) if and only if there are finite vectors \(\lambda\) and \(\mu\geq0\) such that \(E_\omega^{\top}\lambda+F_\delta^{\top}\mu\geq c_\omega\) componentwise and \(d(b,q)^{\top}\lambda<0\). Such a pair explicitly certifies \(\rho_{11}(x,\omega)<\rho_{21}(x,\omega)\) for every common-history law and hence a below-unity value of \(\Psi_\omega(x)\). Symmetrically, every compatible value is above one if and only if there are finite \(\eta\) and \(\kappa\geq0\) such that \(E_\omega^{\top}\eta-F_\delta^{\top}\kappa\leq c_\omega\) and \(d(b,q)^{\top}\eta>0\). When either certificate fails, the corresponding primal optimizer lifts to a compatible full law on the noncertified side.
body.justification: The certificate prices every period, arm, variant, exposure-margin, placebo-stability, and priming-sensitivity row with one coherent set of multipliers and supplies a compatible counterlaw when separation fails.
body.gap: Tomer and Biccler (2022) exhibit mixture-driven temporal movement under specified mechanisms, but do not derive an observable separation theorem over one external-margin common-history sensitivity fiber.
body.consumer: Regulators can audit a robust below-unity conclusion from reported multipliers and recover an attainable counterexample law whenever the certificate fails.
